habitat: Moister areas of evergreen forest, overgrown wasteland and long grass. Occasionally in well-wooded suburban gardens. It is very secretive and is usually located by the call.
summary: A fairly common resident. A tiny, dumpy terrestrial forest bird. The male has a chestnut head, nape and upper breast, rounded buff spots on a dark back, and a chestnut tail barred black. The female is paler and uniform. The call is a long mournful note that rises at the end. The Kemp name Buffspotted Flufftail and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Red-chested Flufftail has streaked upperparts, a mostly black tail, and the male's reddish colour extends onto the mantle and lower breast. It keeps to marshes rather than forest.

viewNotes.note: Chestnut head, nape and upper breast, with rounded buff spots on the dark back.
Rounded buff spots, not streaks. The tail is chestnut barred black.
Paler and uniform. Newman does not give separate colours.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A long, drawn-out mournful 'wooooooooooo-eeeeeeeee', rising at the end, audible from a distance. The grade A call is from KwaZulu-Natal. No Kruger recording was found. The filename is XC952488-Buff-spotted-Flufftail-2024-02-29-05.45.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The female is only described as paler and uniform. The grade A call is from KwaZulu-Natal; no Kruger recording was found. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login xihuhuri is credited. The Kemp name Buffspotted Flufftail and the code NB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^1=2 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 1–4.
